category: former free file host, now a redirect to Send.now

free_tier.stated: Not applicable: userscloud.com redirects to send.now and serves that site's homepage. The successor's terms live's send-now record.

egress.terms: None from this domain; requests are forwarded to send.now.

interface_detail: Whatever send.now offers, now reachable under this hostname by redirect: WebDAV at webdav.send.now, FTP on port 992, and an HTTP API. userscloud.com itself serves no interface.
tooling: None of its own. A client that had a UsersCloud integration now points at Send.now, which has a better tooling story (WebDAV and FTP).
chaining: A rebrand with the old domain kept alive: old index links still resolve, land on the new product, and the new product is a transfer service rather than a PPD host. The chain step disappears but the link does not break.
limits_note: No constraint applies to the old domain; the successor's constraints are recorded under send-now.
binding_note: The old hostname transfers nothing itself.

identity_cost.detail: Nothing is asked for by userscloud.com; the redirect target's free tier needs an email only for a free account.

reliability_note: A redirect is the failure mode this corpus names explicitly: a link checker sees HTTP 200 and a live site, while the host behind the name is a different product with different rules. Any inventory counting UsersCloud separately from Send.now is counting one service twice.
confidence_note: The redirect and landing site were read today. The claim is narrow on purpose: the domain forwards, and it is not an independent service.

evidence.proved: the final URL was https://send.now/ and the body is Send.now's transfer service ('Send large files securely', WebDAV and FTP sections), so UsersCloud no longer hosts anything under its own name

notes: Recorded as dead-with-successor rather than merged, because the slug is what an old link or an old host list will contain. Successor record: send-now.
